rationale:
Layer 2 of save_page_sections preserves an interactive tool that a rebuild's composition dropped. It has TWO arms. The SPLICE arm (the plan named the slot, but produced prose for it) puts the stored bytes into the incoming section, which carries the PLAN's component. The RE-APPEND arm (the plan named the slot NOTHING) builds a whole new section out of the stored row — its bytes, its content_data, its slot name, its provenance stamp — and appends it. Both arms currently take their component id from carriedIdentity(), which returns "" unless the `adopt_unidentified_fragments` flag is armed AND the stored component's function is exactly `adopted-fragment`. A real tool's function is never `adopted-fragment`, so the re-append arm ALWAYS writes component_id NULL, even with the flag armed. enrichSectionsWithComponentIDs ran ~190 lines earlier and never sees the appended entry, so nothing resolves it afterwards. The row is inserted with 13-25KB of working tool and no reference to what produced it.

WHY THAT MATTERS, measured not argued [MEASURED 2026-09-04]: 17 page_components rows fleet-wide across 7 sites hold rendered_html with component_id NULL and build_status<>'removed'. Five are tool slots serving working tools (probed at the body: advertise.co.uk x2, finetuning.uk/playground, idea.uk/tools/funding-fit, loanzy.uk/tools/loan-vs-savings — all 200, all interactive, controls held). THREE of those five were created AFTER bugs_open/385's matcher fix went live on 2026-08-26 (2026-09-03 16:23Z, 16:57Z; 2026-09-04 04:12Z), so this is a LIVE PRODUCER, not a backlog. Every one of the five sits at its page's LAST position and was the LAST row inserted in its write burst — the re-append arm's exact signature (Position: len(sections)+1). That prediction could have come out otherwise and did not, 5/5.

THE HARM IS ON THE RE-RENDER PATH, and it is not 'the tool vanishes'. With component_id NULL, rerender's resolveComponent falls through to the slot-NAME map, which loadComponentSchemas builds as result[function]=ci with NO ORDER BY and last-write-wins. Three of the five orphaned tool slots have 2-3 ACTIVE content_components sharing their function name (advertise's tool-ad-budget-calculator has 2, tool-cpm-cpc-benchmark-comparator has 3, loanzy's tool-loan-vs-savings has 2), so which component renders the page is decided by row order. That is the silent substitution bugs_open/182 exists to prevent, arriving one field along.

WHY THIS IS NOT THE FIX THREE COUNCIL SEATS ALREADY REJECTED, stated plainly because it looks like it. RFC_046 round 1 objected that carrying the stored identity for every interactive section 'would silently keep a legitimately-typed component at its OLD identity when a plan intended to swap it' — three seats, independently. That objection is correct and it is about the SPLICE arm, where an incoming section from the plan is present and expresses an intent. This change does not touch the splice arm. It changes only the RE-APPEND arm, where the plan named the slot NOTHING: there is no incoming section, no plan intent to override, and the appended row is a verbatim copy of a stored row whose component id the copy was dropping. Carrying it preserves a fact the database already holds about the very bytes being re-inserted. A boundary test pins that the splice arm still takes the plan's component, so the rejected widening cannot arrive later by accident.

The active-flag guard is the one non-obvious part and it is not tidiness: a DANGLING id is worse than NULL on the re-render path, because loadComponentSchemasByID drops a row it cannot load and resolveComponent then returns invalidTemplate rather than falling through to the name map, which makes the WHOLE page fatal (rerender_page_sections_action.go). NULL at least falls through. So the id is carried only while it still resolves to an active component.

plan.summary: Split Layer 2's two carry arms apart on the identity axis: the re-append arm keeps the stored row's own component_id (when that component is still active); the splice arm keeps the narrowed, opt-in carriedIdentity the council required.

edits.rationale: The preload already LEFT JOINs content_components for cc.function; it needs cc.is_active too, because carrying a dangling id is worse than carrying none. Reading it here keeps the decision at the point where the row is loaded rather than issuing a second query per section.

grounded_in: save_page_sections_action.go, Layer 2 re-append arm: `ComponentID: carriedIdentity(carryStoredIdentity, p.componentID, p.componentFunction),` with the comment `Today it cannot reach the database — the INSERT resolves a version only when the section also has a component_id, and a re-appended section has none` — the author saw the NULL and read it as a limitation on the STAMP, not as the damage.

adopt_fragment_section.go:173-181 — `func carriedIdentity(armed bool, storedComponentID, storedComponentFunction string) string { if !armed || storedComponentID == "" { return "" }; if storedComponentFunction != adoptedFragmentFunction { return "" }; return storedComponentID }`. adoptedFragmentFunction is the constant "adopted-fragment", so a tool component can never satisfy it — arming the flag would NOT fix this.

adopt_fragment_section_test.go:249 — the objection this change must not reopen, verbatim: `Carrying identity for every interactive section is broader than the diagnosed bug and would silently keep a legitimately-typed component at its OLD identity when a plan intended to swap it — three council seats made that point independently`.

bugs_open/385 §5c joint 5 already NAMED this line — `ComponentID:'' because the RFC_046 carryStoredIdentity opt-in is OFF (default). The enricher at :397 had already run, so nothing ever resolves the appended entry` — but treated it as incidental to the duplication it was diagnosing, and its §4 narrowing (`A non-zero byte_twins_on_page is this bug. A bare component_id IS NULL count is not — it over-reports by 10 out of 11`) is what has kept the orphan class unread since. [MEASURED 2026-09-04] all 17 current orphans have byte_twins=0 and locked_same_slot=0, so 385's own discriminator excludes every one of them.

[MEASURED 2026-09-04] Layer 2's preload predicate (build_status='deployed' AND the interactiveHTMLSQL boolean, printed from the function itself rather than transcribed) selects 378 rows across 371 pages fleet-wide. 385's `[MEASURED 2026-08-25] the armed set is 1 row fleet-wide` was the LOCKED subset, which is 0 today; the re-append arm requires no lock, so the exposed population is three orders of magnitude larger than the number a reader of 385 would carry away.

rerender_page_sections_action.go resolveComponent: `if s.componentID != "" { ... }` then `if ci, ok := schemas[s.slotName]; ok { return ci, false, true }` — the name fallback a NULL id lands in; and plan_sections_action.go loadComponentSchemas `result[ci.Function] = ci` over a query with no ORDER BY, so with 2-3 active same-function components the winner is row order.

Package tests pass except TestFindingCodeScanEveryWriteIsRegistered and TestTemplateExecutorsAreDeclared, which are pre-existing at HEAD from the 440 lane (fail_work_item_message_template.go, committed 83407cd37) and unrelated to this change.
plan.risks:
A re-appended section now reaches resolveComponentVersionID with a non-nil component id, which the existing test TestLayer2_ReappendedToolCarriesTheStoredStamp explicitly anticipated ('This arm cannot reach the database today ... exists so that the two arms cannot silently disagree once the identity round lands'). Verified query-neutral: with carriedVersionID empty and renderedSHA empty the resolver returns ('', false) before issuing any query (save_sections_component_version.go:84-94), so no new DB traffic and no new sqlmock expectations.

A page that legitimately wants its tool RE-TYPED by a rebuild will now keep the old component on the re-append arm. Judged acceptable because the re-append arm fires only when the plan does not name the slot at all — a plan that wants to re-type a slot names it, which is the splice arm, which is unchanged.

This does not repair the 17 existing orphans; it stops new ones. The repair is separate and is complicated by the fact that 3 of the 5 tool orphans have 2-3 active same-function components, so the obvious slot_name->cc.function repair is NOT unique and would bind an arbitrary one. Recorded in bugs_open/479 rather than guessed at here.

The change reads cc.is_active at preload time; a component deactivated between preload and insert would still be carried. The window is milliseconds and the failure mode is the pre-change behaviour (a dangling id), so no guard is proposed.
